blocks.prompt: 1 A student downloads a free game from an unknown website; soon the computer slows down and unknown programs start running. (i) Explain the risks of downloading suspicious software and unsafe browsing that may explain this. (ii) Explain how troubleshooting and preventive measures should be applied, and how such a problem can be avoided in future. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Risks of suspicious downloads and unsafe browsing:
1. Downloading programs or files from unknown websites can harm the computer or steal information.
2. Some downloads hide viruses or spyware that collect data without permission; spyware secretly collects user information, and a virus can damage or delete data.
3. Unexpected system slowdowns and unknown programs running are signs of suspicious activity, so the game has probably brought malware with it.
4. Unsafe browsing, such as visiting fake websites or clicking unknown links, can also lead to scams or identity theft.

(ii) Troubleshooting and preventive measures:
1. Troubleshooting: when a security issue is found, find its cause and how to fix it (check system logs and use scanning tools).
2. Preventive measures: install firewalls, antivirus and anti-malware; update the software; change the passwords; remove the harmful files.
3. In some cases, restore data from backups.
4. Document the problem and the steps taken, so it does not happen again.

Avoiding it in future: check sources before downloading, use antivirus tools for extra protection and keep safe browsing habits; these keep both devices and data secure.

book_ref.quote: Downloading programs or files from unknown websites can harm your computer or steal your information.

blocks.prompt: 2 Using the chapter's examples of Instagram, WhatsApp and signing up on a social platform, explain four steps a student can take to protect his or her privacy online. Also differentiate between privacy settings and a privacy policy. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Privacy and security settings help users control how their personal information is used and shared online; a privacy policy explains how a website or app collects, stores and uses the information.

Four steps:
1. Instagram: make the account private so that only approved followers can see the posts; turn off location sharing; enable two-factor authentication for extra account security.
2. WhatsApp: choose who can see the profile photo (everyone, only contacts, or nobody) and disable read receipts (blue ticks) so others cannot see whether messages have been read.
3. Signing up: read the privacy policy before creating an account or agreeing to terms. It explains what data may be collected (name, email address, location, browsing activity, app usage) and whether it is shared with advertisers or third-party services; then decide whether to share the data or not.
4. Review and limit: limit app permissions and regularly review and update settings, because platforms often change their privacy rules.

Difference (see table).

book_ref.quote: By reviewing these policies, users can decide whether to share personal data or not.

blocks.prompt: 3 Students often work in groups online. (i) What is safe online collaboration? (ii) Explain how Google Docs, Google Workspace and Google Meet can be used safely for group work. (iii) What is digital etiquette? Explain it with the example of a class group chat. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Online collaboration allows people to work together using digital tools from any location. Safe online collaboration means using secure platforms and following safety rules when sharing files or communicating online, so that personal and school data stay protected. It builds trust and ensures productive and respectful teamwork.

(ii) Using platforms safely:
1. Google Docs: share the document only with trusted classmates, and set the permission to "View only" instead of "Edit" if others only need to read it; this protects the document from unwanted changes.
2. Google Workspace: share a project file only with selected classmates through restricted access. Secure platforms such as Google Workspace and Microsoft Teams use encrypted communication and access controls to safeguard data.
3. Google Meet: use it for secure online classes where only authorized participants are allowed to join.
Choosing trusted and approved platforms protects information and reduces cyber risks.

(iii) Digital etiquette means communicating politely, respectfully and clearly in online environments: using appropriate language, respecting others' opinions, not sharing private information and not misusing communication tools. Example: in a class group chat, students respect others' opinions and avoid spam messages, unrelated memes or jokes during serious academic discussions. This keeps the group useful, respectful and focused on learning.

book_ref.quote: Students learn to work responsibly in virtual groups while protecting personal and school data.

blocks.prompt: 4 Cyber threats have become common in daily life. (i) Define cybersecurity awareness and cyber threats. (ii) Explain how a user can recognize cyber threats early and avoid most attacks in daily online use. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Cybersecurity awareness means understanding how to protect computers, networks and data from attacks. Cyber threats are actions or programs that target computers and networks to cause harm, such as stealing information, damaging systems or interrupting online services.

(ii) Recognizing and avoiding threats:
1. Recognize threats first: understanding how threats work helps users recognize early warning signs; recognizing threats is the first step toward protecting digital systems.
2. Watch for warning signs: unexpected system slowdowns, unknown programs running or strange network traffic; checking system logs and using scanning tools helps find them.
3. Safe browsing: avoid fake websites and unknown links, and be cautious with emails, because phishing (one of the most common attacks) uses fake emails or websites to steal passwords.
4. Antivirus software: install it to protect the computer from malware and other threats.
5. Avoid public Wi-Fi for online banking or other sensitive work, because public networks may not be secure.
6. Being aware and knowing how to detect, prevent and respond to threats keeps personal and organizational data secure.

book_ref.quote: Understanding how threats work helps users recognize early warning signs.

blocks.prompt: 5 Data must be kept private when stored and when sent. (i) Define data protection and cryptography. (ii) Explain encryption and decryption with an example. (iii) Explain the secure methods for transmitting and storing data. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Data protection means keeping digital information safe from unauthorized access, loss or damage; it ensures that only the right people can view or use the data. Cryptography is the science of securing information so that only authorized users can understand it.

(ii) Cryptography consists of two core concepts:
1. Encryption changes readable data into coded text using a specific key.
2. Decryption converts the coded text back into its original form when needed.
Example: when a message is sent online, encryption makes it unreadable to anyone who tries to intercept it, so the information remains private during transmission; the authorized receiver decrypts it to read it. Cryptography is widely used in secure websites, online banking and messaging apps.

(iii) Secure methods for transmitting and storing data (data must be protected when stored and when sent):
1. Encrypted connections (like HTTPS) keep information safe during transmission.
2. Cloud storage services use encryption to prevent unauthorized access to saved files.
3. Regular backups protect data from loss caused by system failure or attacks.
Following these methods ensures that important data remains safe and reliable.

book_ref.quote: This process ensures that information remains private during transmission.

blocks.prompt: 6 Hackers look for weak points in systems. (i) What is meant by detecting and preventing intrusions? (ii) What are vulnerabilities and suspicious activities, and how are they identified? (iii) Explain how troubleshooting and preventive measures are applied when a security issue is found. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Detecting and preventing intrusions means identifying and stopping unauthorized access to a computer or network. Intrusions occur when hackers exploit weaknesses to steal data or damage systems. Monitoring tools and security software track unusual activity that might indicate an attack; early detection prevents major losses, and staying alert and updating security measures maintain protection.

(ii) Vulnerabilities are weaknesses in software, hardware or user behavior that hackers can exploit. Suspicious activities may include unexpected system slowdowns, unknown programs running or strange network traffic. They are identified by regularly checking system logs and using scanning tools; recognizing patterns of unusual behavior allows quick action, and fixing vulnerabilities early reduces the chance of successful attacks.

(iii) Troubleshooting and preventive measures:
1. Troubleshooting determines the cause of the issue and how to fix it.
2. Preventive measures: installing firewalls, antiviruses and anti-malware, updating software, changing passwords or removing harmful files.
3. In some cases data must be restored from backups.
4. Documenting the problem and the steps taken helps prevent it from happening again.

book_ref.quote: Students learn how early detection prevents major losses and keeps systems running safely.

blocks.prompt: 7 Technology lets people work together from different places. (i) Define digital collaboration and equity in computing. (ii) Explain the importance of teamwork and communication in digital environments. (iii) Explain how real-time collaboration tools help teams, naming the platforms given in the chapter. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Digital collaboration means using technology to work together on shared tasks, projects or ideas; it lets people connect and contribute from different places using the internet. Equity in computing ensures that everyone, regardless of background or ability, can participate and access digital resources equally. Combining the two creates inclusive and effective learning and working environments.

(ii) Teamwork and communication in digital environments:
1. Teamwork needs clear communication and trust; when everyone contributes ideas and listens to others, projects run smoothly.
2. Effective communication prevents misunderstandings and keeps all members informed about progress.
3. Group chats, emails and video calls help teams stay connected.
4. Good teamwork encourages creativity, cooperation and shared responsibility; working online also prepares students for modern workplaces where remote work is common.

(iii) Real-time collaboration tools allow multiple users to work on the same project at the same time. Platforms such as Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams and Zoom make sharing documents, chatting and meeting online easier. Teams organize tasks, edit files together and stay updated instantly; this saves time and reduces errors by keeping everyone aligned.

book_ref.quote: It allows people to connect and contribute from different places using the internet.

blocks.prompt: 8 Technology should be usable by everyone. (i) What is meant by designing for equity and accessibility, and by equal access? Name the challenges some people face. (ii) Explain how developers can create inclusive applications for diverse users. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Designing for equity and accessibility ensures that technology can be used by everyone, including people with different abilities and backgrounds.
Equal access means that every person should have the same opportunity to use technology and the internet. It includes access to reliable devices, internet connections and digital skills.
Challenges: some people face disabilities, language barriers or lack of resources. Understanding these issues helps developers and organizations design solutions that reach everyone, so no one is left behind in the digital world. Accessible design benefits people with disabilities and improves usability for everyone.

(ii) Creating inclusive applications (designed to meet the needs of different types of users):
1. Screen readers for the visually impaired.
2. Subtitles for videos.
3. Multiple language options.
4. Simple layouts and clear text, which make apps easier for beginners.
5. Testing designs with a variety of users to ensure accessibility for all.
Inclusive digital tools support equality and improve the overall user experience.

book_ref.quote: Understanding these issues helps developers and organizations design solutions that reach everyone.

blocks.prompt: 9 Effective collaboration helps teams complete tasks successfully. Explain the five strategies for effective collaboration given in the chapter. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Effective collaboration: teamwork becomes stronger when everyone understands their responsibilities and communicates clearly; planning, organizing and sharing ideas move projects forward without confusion, and members learn to respect different opinions and work toward a common goal.

1. Assigning roles: clear roles help each member know exactly what to do, e.g. one person handles research, another organizes information, and someone else prepares the final presentation.
2. Managing tasks: creating checklists or timelines helps the team stay on track and avoid delays.
3. Setting team goals: shared goals give everyone a direction to work toward and encourage cooperation; when roles and goals are clear, teamwork becomes easier and more efficient.
4. Reflecting on collaborative experiences: after a project, students think about what went well and what could be improved, identifying strengths (good communication) and weaknesses (missed deadlines).
5. Discussion to improve teamwork: discussing these experiences helps students learn from mistakes and become better team players; it encourages respect and understanding and, over time, leads to stronger teamwork.

book_ref.quote: Planning, organizing, and sharing ideas allow group projects to move forward without confusion.

blocks.prompt: 10 Entrepreneurs turn ideas into businesses. (i) Explain the characteristics of successful entrepreneurs. (ii) Describe how entrepreneurship is growing in Pakistan's digital economy. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Characteristics of successful entrepreneurs:
1. Creative: they always look for new ideas to solve problems.
2. Hardworking: they remain committed to achieving their goals.
3. Confident and willing to take calculated risks (most successful entrepreneurs are not born risk-takers; they develop risk-taking skills through experience).
4. Strong decision-making and problem-solving skills.
5. Adaptable: they adjust to changing market conditions and customer needs.

(ii) Entrepreneurship in Pakistan and the digital economy:
1. It is growing rapidly due to increased access to the internet and mobile technology.
2. Many young people start online businesses through social media, e-commerce platforms and freelancing websites.
3. The digital economy creates new jobs in software development, digital marketing and online services.
4. Government and private initiatives support startups and innovation.
This growth helps improve the country's economy and encourages youth to become job creators instead of job seekers.

book_ref.quote: Successful entrepreneurs are creative and always look for new ideas to solve problems.

blocks.prompt: 11 Every business starts from a real need. (i) What is meant by identifying business opportunities? (ii) Explain how technology solves real-world problems, with examples. (iii) Explain how entrepreneurs recognize market needs and customer demands. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Identifying business opportunities means finding problems in society that can be solved through products or services. Entrepreneurs observe daily life to understand customer needs and market demands. Technology helps discover opportunities such as online education, e-commerce and digital services. In Pakistan, agriculture, healthcare and education provide many opportunities for digital business ideas (Figure 9.4 shows technology-based solutions for education, healthcare, agriculture and business as four separate areas).

(ii) Solving real-world problems through technology: technology lets entrepreneurs solve problems faster and more efficiently and create digital solutions in education, healthcare, agriculture and business. Examples:
1. Online learning platforms help students study from home.
2. Mobile apps support farmers in improving crop production.
3. Digital payment systems make financial transactions easier and safer.

(iii) Recognizing market needs means understanding what people want and what problems they face. Entrepreneurs study customer behavior, preferences and trends; surveys, feedback and online data help identify gaps in the market. Meeting customer needs effectively leads to customer satisfaction and business success; in the digital economy, analyzing online trends and user feedback is very important.

book_ref.quote: Successful entrepreneurs focus on solving real-world problems in innovative ways.

blocks.prompt: 12 A student wants to start selling handmade items online. Explain how she can use the three kinds of digital platforms for entrepreneurship (social media, e-commerce platforms, freelancing and remote work) and the benefits of each. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
Digital platforms provide entrepreneurs with tools to start, manage and grow their businesses online; they include social media, e-commerce websites and freelancing marketplaces (shown in Figure 9.5).

1. Social media: helps in promoting products and reaching a large audience quickly. She can show her items to many people and build awareness of her business.
2. E-commerce platforms and online marketplaces: allow businesses to sell products and services over the internet and connect sellers with customers without the need for a physical store. Customers can browse products, compare prices and place orders online. Buying and selling becomes easier, faster and accessible to a wider audience, and costs are reduced while market reach expands.
3. Freelancing and remote work: freelancing websites let people offer their skills and services to clients globally, in areas such as graphic design, writing, programming and digital marketing; remote work lets people work for companies from home or any location with an internet connection. These give flexibility, independent income and global access to job markets (e.g. she could also offer design services).

Together these platforms make entrepreneurship easier and more accessible.

book_ref.quote: Digital platforms provide entrepreneurs with tools to start, manage, and grow their businesses online

blocks.prompt: 13 A digital business needs a clear plan. (i) Explain the steps of planning a small digital business and the basic business planning concepts. (ii) Explain budgeting and resource management. (iii) Why are teamwork and communication essential in startups? (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Planning a small digital business means organizing ideas into a clear and workable plan:
1. Identify a product or service that meets customer needs.
2. Decide the target audience, pricing and method of delivery using digital platforms.
3. Prepare a basic budget to manage costs and expected income.
Basic planning concepts: set clear goals for what the business wants to achieve, understand the target market, decide how to deliver value to customers, and plan resources such as time, money and skills. A simple business plan organizes ideas and gives direction (most failed startups do not have a clear plan).

(ii) Budgeting and resource management involve planning how money, time and other resources will be used. A budget helps entrepreneurs estimate costs, set prices and manage income and expenses. Resource management ensures that materials, skills and tools are used efficiently without waste. Together they maintain profitability and support long-term success.

(iii) Team members share ideas, responsibilities and skills to achieve common goals. Effective communication avoids misunderstandings and improves decision-making; clear coordination through meetings, messaging apps and online tools ensures a smooth workflow. Strong teamwork and communication increase productivity and help the business grow.

book_ref.quote: Planning a small digital business involves organizing ideas into a clear and workable plan.

blocks.prompt: 14 New technologies are changing business. (i) Define innovation and explain its role in digital entrepreneurship. (ii) Explain how emerging technologies and AI, apps and digital services help businesses. (iii) Name the career pathways in technology entrepreneurship. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Innovation means creating new and improved ideas, products or services that solve problems in better ways. It helps digital businesses grow and stay competitive and plays a key role in developing products and services that meet changing market needs. Future opportunities are expanding because of AI, mobile apps and online platforms, creating new career paths and business ideas.

(ii) Emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, blockchain and mobile applications are transforming entrepreneurship: they help create smarter, faster and more efficient solutions, reduce costs, improve productivity and enable global reach; startups use them for innovative products that meet modern customer needs.
1. AI helps entrepreneurs analyze data, understand customer behavior and improve decision-making.
2. Mobile apps make it easier to reach customers, sell products and provide services quickly.
3. Digital services such as online payments, cloud storage and marketing tools improve efficiency and reduce costs.
Together they make businesses more competitive in the digital economy.

(iii) Career pathways: startup founder; freelancer in programming, graphic design or digital marketing; app developer; e-commerce manager; online consultant; innovator creating new digital solutions for real-world problems.

book_ref.quote: By adopting innovation, individuals can build successful and future-ready digital businesses.

blocks.prompt: 15 Computing has ethical effects. (i) Explain the ethical use of technology. (ii) Explain intellectual property and data ownership and how they should be respected. (iii) Explain the consequences of unethical digital behavior. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Ethical use of technology involves acting responsibly and avoiding harm through digital actions. It includes respecting privacy, fairness and proper handling of information. Decisions in technology should consider the effects on people, organizations and society. Following ethical guidelines maintains trust and safety online; copying online content without permission can violate both copyright laws and digital ethics.

(ii) Intellectual property refers to creative work such as software, music or writing. Data ownership refers to the right to control personal information. Respecting these rights means avoiding copying, sharing or using work without permission, and protecting personal and sensitive information instead of misusing it. Legal and ethical respect for them encourages fairness and protects creators and users.

(iii) Unethical digital behavior includes hacking, spreading false information and cyberbullying. Such actions cause harm, damage reputations and lead to legal consequences; even small actions online may have significant effects. Understanding these outcomes encourages responsible conduct, and maintaining ethical standards ensures a safer and more trustworthy online environment.

book_ref.quote: Following ethical guidelines helps maintain trust and safety online.

blocks.prompt: 16 Laws protect people and data in the digital world. (i) What are data privacy laws, and what is cybercrime? (ii) Compare the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) with Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (PECA) 2016 in a table. (8 marks)
blocks.explanation:
(i) Data privacy laws are legal rules that protect how personal data is collected, stored, used and shared; they ensure that personal and sensitive information is handled responsibly. Cybercrime refers to illegal activities carried out using computers, networks or the internet, such as hacking, identity theft and online fraud. These laws protect individuals, organizations and society, help prevent legal issues and encourage trust in online systems.

(ii) Comparison of GDPR and PECA 2016 (see table).

book_ref.quote: Many countries and companies follow similar standards to ensure data privacy globally.
